tasks.q: Which of these is a requirement of an algorithm?
a: Every step is unambiguous and the whole thing finishes
It must be written in Python
It must be under twenty lines
tasks.fb: Language and length are irrelevant; clarity and finishing are not.

tasks.q: Why is 'stir until it looks right' not a good algorithm step?
a: It is ambiguous: different people would do different things

tasks.q: Put these steps for finding the largest number in a list into a sensible order.
steps: Set the largest so far to the first item
If it is bigger than the largest so far, make it the new largest
Repeat until the end of the list
tasks.fb: Notice it works for any list, of any length: that is the point.

tasks.q: Why is an algorithm more useful than solving one case by hand?
a: It works for every similar problem, not just the one in front of you
tasks.fb: Generality is what makes it worth writing down.

tasks.q: For a cash machine, is each one an input, a process or an output?
items: The PIN typed by the customer
tasks.fb: Data in, work done, results back out.

tasks.q: A program asks for two numbers, adds them and shows the total. What is the process?
tasks.fb: Asking is input; showing is output; the addition is the process.

tasks.q: Put these stages of solving a problem into order.
steps: Decide what the output should be
Work out what input is needed
Write the steps that turn the input into the output
Test the steps with an example by hand
tasks.fb: Testing on paper catches most mistakes before any code is written.

a: It tells you what the program must produce, which decides what input and steps you need
The exam asks for it first
tasks.fb: Working backwards from the answer keeps the steps focused.

tasks.q: Put the steps of a pick-up sticks game into order.
steps: Ask the current player how many to take, between one and three
Take that many from the pile
If sticks remain, swap to the other player and repeat
When the pile is empty, the player who took the last stick loses
tasks.fb: Set up, repeat a turn, check the end condition, announce the result.

tasks.q: Where does the algorithm need a decision rather than a step?
a: Checking whether any sticks are left, which decides whether to carry on
tasks.fb: Decisions are where the path through an algorithm branches.

tasks.q: Which is the better algorithm step?
a: IF the amount entered is more than the balance THEN show an error
tasks.fb: Unambiguous, with a clear condition and a clear result.

tasks.q: A student writes an algorithm with no way of stopping. What is wrong?
a: An algorithm must always finish, so it isn't an algorithm yet
tasks.fb: An endless loop is a classic exam mistake.

tasks.q: For a library self-service kiosk, is each one an input, a process or an output?
items: The barcode scanned from the book
The date the book is due back
Checking whether the borrower owes a fine
Working out the due date from today
The receipt printed for the borrower
Marking the book as on loan in the database
The message shown on the screen
tasks.fb: Data in, work done, results back out: the split earns marks in almost every scenario question.

info.title: Where the word comes from
info.text: Algorithm comes from the name of the ninth-century scholar al-Khwarizmi, whose book on calculation reached Europe in translation.

info.title: Older than computers
info.text: Euclid wrote an algorithm for the greatest common divisor around 300 BC. It is still taught, and still works.

info.title: Ambiguity kills
info.text: A famous early spacecraft was lost because two teams used different units. The steps were clear to each of them, and to nobody else.

info.title: Terminating matters
info.text: Deciding whether an arbitrary program will ever stop is provably impossible in general, a result from Alan Turing in 1936.

info.title: Same problem, many algorithms
info.text: Sorting a list can be done a dozen different ways. You meet three of them later in this topic.

info.title: Exam tip
info.text: If a question says 'write an algorithm', numbered steps in plain English earn the marks. You are not required to use a language.
